extraction.name: Science Question Answering (SCIENCE QA)
extraction.description: A multimodal multiple-choice science question dataset containing 21,208 examples with diverse science topics and annotations of answers with corresponding lectures and explanations. It covers natural science, social science, and language science, with multimodal contexts including text and images.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu; Swaroop Mishra; Tony Xia; Liang Qiu; Kai-Wei Chang; Song-Chun Zhu; Oyvind Tafjord; Peter Clark; Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan. Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. NeurIPS 2022.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the SCIENCE QA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in K-12 education. The authors downloaded the original science problems and extracted individual components such as questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions based on heuristic rules. They manually removed invalid questions, including questions with only one choice, faulty data, and duplicates. If multiple correct answers applied, they kept only one correct answer. They also shuffled answer options and used semi-automated scripts to reformat lectures and solutions. Incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts after review with a data exploration tool.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Original science problems sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, including questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions aligned with California Common Core Content Standards.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors extracted components from downloaded problems using heuristic rules, manually removed invalid and duplicated questions, kept only one correct answer when multiple correct answers applied, shuffled answer options, and used semi-automated scripts to reformat lectures and solutions. Incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual components were extracted from original problems based on heuristic rules. Invalid questions were removed, including those with only one choice, faulty data, and duplicates. Answer options were shuffled. Semi-automated scripts reformatted lectures and solutions so special structures such as tables and lists were distinguishable from simple text passages. For modeling, image captions were generated for images and questions without context used an empty string as context text.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations. The lecture provides general knowledge introducing background information for solving similar problems, while the explanation reveals a specific reason for the answer. Incorrect annotations in the collected dataset were manually revised by experts. Human evaluation of generated explanations was conducted by AMT workers who judged whether explanations were relevant, correct, and complete, with final human scores determined by majority vote.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human evaluation of generated explanations, each batch was assigned to 3 workers and final human scores were determined by majority vote. The paper reports relevance, correctness, completeness, and whether an explanation meets the gold standard of being relevant, correct, and complete.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For the human performance study, only Amazon Mechanical Turk workers who obtained a high school or higher degree and passed qualification examples were qualified.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules; semi-automated scripts; data exploration tool; ViT-GPT2 image captioning tool
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code are available at https://scienceqa.github.io. SCIENCE QA is available for non-commercial research purposes only and the copyright belongs to the original authors.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The collected data does not contain personally identifiable information or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is proposed to diagnose multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. It is intended to benefit follow-up research and real-world applications, including multimodal learning, multi-hop reasoning, general artificial intelligence, and K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The authors state they adhere to the goal of AI for the common good and that antisocial data points will be removed based on feedback.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: After careful examination, the authors state they have not found improper content such as pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations through error analysis. Failure cases include models failing to understand multimodal inputs, lacking domain-specific knowledge, and generating wrong chain-of-thought explanations with irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete information. Image captions used as visual input lack fine-grained semantics and usually do not work well for diagrams. Current models still lag behind human performance by a large margin.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training, validation, and testing, with random splits of 60:20:20 into 12,726 training, 4,241 validation, and 4,241 test examples. It is proposed as a benchmark for multimodal question answering, multi-hop reasoning, explanation generation, and development of reliable models that generate coherent chains of thought. It is available for non-commercial research purposes only.
